name: XENO STORE companions
author: XENOKING
_notes: Owner-curated catalog of scene payloads that make XENO STORE one-click (SPEC §17.16). XENO STORE downloads the file to /data/xeno-store/payloads/<id>.elf, checks the sha256 and sends the bytes to the local ELF loader on 127.0.0.1:9021. It never loads code in-process.

Every 'url' is the payload author's own GitHub release asset, pinned to one release with its sha256 and size (verified 2026-10-15). XENO STORE never mirrors or rehosts these files; to move an entry to a newer release, replace url, version, size and sha256 together (sha256sum <file>).
An entry whose author publishes no downloadable asset is marked "unavailable": true with an 'unavailableReason': it stays listed for its credits and never installs.

'kind' is matched by the readiness checklist and the engine (shadowmount → Launch ShadowMountPlus now, dpi → package installer fallback, np-signin/np-signout → Accounts screen, dumper → Library 'Back up this game to a dump', saves → Garlic Save Manager, started on demand to re-sign community saves).

payloads.name: ShadowMountPlus
payloads.notes: By drakmor (GPL-3.0), the evolution of VoidWhisper's ShadowMount. Mounts exFAT / FFPKG / FFPFS(C) dumps from <drive>/homebrew/ and shows them on the home screen; XENO STORE asks it to rescan on 127.0.0.1:10101 (1.7 and newer) after every download. Needed for image formats; PKG installs work without it.

payloads.name: Package installer daemon (DPI)
payloads.notes: ezRemote DPI by cy33hc (GPL-3.0), modelled on etaHEN's DPI: a background installer that takes http(s) package URLs on 127.0.0.1:9040 (XENO TOOL ships a plain-C port of it). XENO STORE installs PKGs natively first and falls back to this daemon when the native call is refused on your firmware.

payloads.name: kstuff
payloads.notes: Kernel patches by sleirsgoevy (ps5-kstuff in sleirsgoevy/ps4jb-payloads), builds for newer firmware maintained by EchoStretch. They let fake packages (FPKG) run: load it once per boot before installing or launching FPKG titles. Firmware support follows the upstream project — read its README for your firmware.

payloads.name: NP fake sign-in
payloads.notes: By earthonion (the project now lives at git.etawen.dev/earthonion/np-fake-signin; this is its GitHub release). Makes the console believe PSN is signed in for the foreground user so trophies and some online checks work offline. Activate the profile first (Settings → Accounts), then send this payload. Undo it in Settings → Users and Accounts → Other → Sign out. The repository has no licence file, so XENO STORE only downloads the author's release on your console.

payloads.name: NP fake sign-out
payloads.unavailableReason: earthonion publishes no sign-out payload (np-fake-signin 1.1 ships only the sign-in ELF). Sign out from Settings → Users and Accounts → Other → Sign out instead.
payloads.notes: Reverting NP fake sign-in needs no payload: use Settings → Users and Accounts → Other → Sign out before signing in to the real PlayStation Network again.

payloads.name: PS5 App Dumper
payloads.notes: By EchoStretch, based on logic-68's pfsmnt-dumper. Dumps an installed game's files to a USB drive attached to the console (never over the network) and serves a web page (port 8081 by default) to pick the title, the drive and the settings. Library → 'Back up this game to a dump' launches it. Large games take a long time; keep the console awake.

payloads.name: Garlic Save Manager
payloads.notes: Save decrypt / re-sign tool by earthonion on 127.0.0.1:8082. XENO STORE installs community saves through its import API (re-signed for your profile) and makes shareable decrypted exports with it; when it is not running, XENO STORE starts a copy found on the console or downloads this release. The repository has no licence file, so XENO STORE never rehosts it: it downloads this exact release from the author's GitHub on your console (sha256 checked).
